proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12370 śāka potherb, vegetable gives Prakrit sāga/sāya and Pali sāka. The survey sag/sāg vegetable responses retain the voiced stop of the sāga branch; the isolated sãg nasalisation is preserved as a regional qualification. This is a comparative vegetable-family link, with local Indo-Aryan transmission unresolved. Exact response: sag.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 1341 ārdraka explicitly gives Nepali aduwā dried ginger, alongside Kumaoni ādo, Bengali/Assamese ādā and Gujarati ādũ ginger. The selected aduva/əduwa responses fit the Nepali-type extended form; survey ginger does not specify dried versus fresh. The initial reduced vowel and v/w notation are retained, with local Indo-Aryan transmission unresolved. Exact response: aduva.

The selected bare kaṭ and Bengali kaʈa fit this cutting verb. Source vowel length and ordinary Bengali verbal ending are retained; local Indo-Aryan transmission remains open. Exact response: kaṭ.
